title: Preemptive Fallback and Burst Hedging for GPU Pools (Runbook)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This runbook defines the operational pattern we call "burst hedging" and the associated preemptive fallback procedures for multi-tenant GPU pools. Burst hedging aims to keep customer-facing latency SLOs stable during sudden demand spikes while minimizing cost and minimizing impact from spot/preemptible GPU eviction. This doc covers detection, automated mitigations, manual runbook steps, IaC/CI/CD commands to enact policy changes, and post-incident reconciliation.

Scope and audience:

- Scope: Redwood-hosted GPU clusters (both dedicated and burst-capable pools), warm-pool instances, cross-account burst lanes, and autoscaler policies.
- Audience: Oncall infra engineers, SREs responsible for GPU fleet, infra platform owners, and Product enabling for Dedicated capacity customers.

Terminology:

- Burst hedging: a proactive reserve strategy that keeps a small amount of capacity or warm instances across heterogeneous pools to absorb sudden spikes.
- Preemptible/spot: lower-cost GPU instances subject to eviction.
- Warm pool: provisioned instances kept in a ready state for fast attach/start (minutes).
- Hedging credit: internal accounting token used to temporarily cover user requests processed by hedged capacity (used for billing reconciliation).

Indicators and alerting thresholds:

Primary signals to trigger this runbook (automated first, manual fallback second):

1) Per-model tail latency 95/99 increases beyond SLO by 30% for a sustained 2 minutes (metric: model.latency.p95).
2) Queue depth increase > 40% baseline for more than 60s (metric: inference.queue.depth).
3) Warm-pool attach failures > 2% over 5 minutes (metric: warmpool.attach.err_rate).
4) Spot eviction rate crosses 12% / 5m (metric: spot.eviction.rate).

When any of the above occur, the autoscaler will first attempt automated hedging steps (section: Automated mitigation). If those fail or if the incident severity escalates, follow the Manual runbook.

SLOs and guardrails:

- Target: 99th percentile request latency <= 1.2x baseline SLO during 99% of spikes.
- Cost guardrail: total burst hedging spend capped at 15% of hourly GPU spend for that tenant/availability zone.
- Eviction fallback: if eviction rate > 20% sustained, automatically shift hedging weight to dedicated-pool fallbacks.

Automated mitigation (preferred path) - what the control plane does automatically:

- Step A: Short-term prefix caching. If model request patterns match recent prefixes, route requests to the cache layer to reduce token generation demand.
- Step B: Warm-pool attach expansion. Trigger small warm-pool scale-up (default: +3 instances) in nearest AZs with healthy attach latency < 120s.
- Step C: Cross-pool hedging. Re-route a fraction of traffic (default 10%) to heterogeneous pools (e.g., mixed precision or quantized variants) using runtime routing policy.
- Step D: Local failover to pre-warmed CPU-backed decoders for ultra-low-throughput bursts where quality loss is acceptable (feature flag controlled).

If automated steps do not bring metrics back within thresholds within 180s, escalate to manual procedures.

Manual runbook (ordered actions for oncall):

1) Acknowledge the incident in PagerDuty, tag with label: gpu-burst-hedge.
2) Run quick triage (2 min): check the following dashboards and logs:
   - GPU pool utilization and per-tenant credits dashboard
   - Warm-pool attach logs: /dashboards/warmpool/attach
   - Spot eviction telemetry: metric spot.eviction.rate
3) If queue depth or latency is still elevated, execute the hedging policy expansion command (requires Infra Approver scope):

   CLI: (gcloud AWS examples vary per provider)

   # Expand warm pool across AZs (example)
   infractl warmpool scale --pool-id gpu-warmpool-eu-west-1 --delta 3 --timeout 10m

   # Increase cross-pool hedging weight (10 -> 25%)
   infractl routing set-hedge-weight --service inference-api --from 0.10 --to 0.25 --target-pools "quantized,half-precision" --ttl 15m

4) If warmpool attaches are failing, remediate attach failures first: check the attach-controller logs on the control plane (service: attach-controller) and rotate credentials if CA push failed. Commands:

   kubectl -n infra logs deploy/attach-controller | tail -n 200

   # If credential expiration is suspected (example):
   aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id infra/warmpool/attach-creds --query SecretString | jq .

5) If preemptible eviction is the root cause, trigger temporary reduce-spot-policy to shift weights to dedicated or reserved capacity:

   # Update autoscaler policy via terraform plan/apply (use canary first)
   cd infra/terraform/modules/autoscaler-policies
   terraform workspace select staging
   terraform apply -var='adjust_spot_weight=true' -var='spot_weight=0.15' -auto-approve

6) If customer tier SLA is impacted (alerts from dedicated customers), immediately enable priority hedging for that tenant only and notify account owner via Slack channel #enterprise-dedicated-alerts.

Operational ownership and contact list:

- First responder: gpu-fleet-sre@redwood.ai (PagerDuty: infra-gpu)
- Platform owner: infra-platform (Slack: #infra-platform)
- Attach-controller owner: runtime-core
- Warm-pool CI owner: ci-cd-gpu-team

Configuration parameters (summary table):

| Key                         | Default | Notes |
|----------------------------:|:-------:|:------|
| warmpool.scale_delta        | "3"    | number of instances to add when hedging triggers |
| hedging.default_weight      | "0.10" | fraction of traffic routed to hedged pools |
| hedging.max_hourly_spend_pct| "0.15" | cost cap per-hour fraction |
| spot.eviction_threshold_pct | "0.12" | eviction rate to trigger hedging |
| hedging.ttl_minutes        | "15"   | how long routing changes persist by default |

Example Terraform snippet (policy flag):

```hcl
module "autoscaler_policy" {
  source = "../../../modules/autoscaler-policies"

  name                   = "inference-hedging-policy"
  warmpool_scale_delta   = 3
  hedging_default_weight = 0.10
  hedging_ttl_minutes    = 15
  spot_eviction_threshold_pct = 12
}
```

CI/CD and safety gates for policy changes:

- Any change to autoscaler-policies module must:
  1) Pass unit tests and a smoke canary in the staging region (50 requests/s simulation).
  2) Include a cost-estimate check in the PR (pipeline step: cost-estimator).
  3) Be annotated with rollout ramp-up schedule (0 -> full weight over 30m minimum).

- Emergency patching: a small emergency PR can be merged with 1 approver and a short-lived canary toggle, but must be followed by a post-merge retrospective within 24 hours.

Runbook rollback and cleanup steps:

1) After resolving demand spike, revert hedging weight to baseline via infractl routing set-hedge-weight --to 0.10 or via terraform reverting the autoscaler var.
2) Drain any transient warm-pools if they will remain idle > 30m: infractl warmpool drain --pool-id <id> --grace 300s.
3) Trigger cost reconciliation job to consume hedging credits and allocate costs to tenants: infractl billing reconcile-hedge --window "-1h".

Diagnostic checklist for post-incident review (always run within 48 hours):

- What triggered the spike? (product launch, eval batch, runaway retry loop, external traffic surge)
- Were automated mitigations timely? If not, why (attach latency, IAM, or capacity)?
- How much hedging spend was used (USD and % of hourly spend)?
- Which tenants were impacted and was the billing reconciliation correct?
- Do we need to change hedging defaults (warmpool.delta, hedging.weight, or cost cap)?

Post-incident actions and owners (examples):

- Adjust hedging.safe_defaults if observed overspend: owner infra-platform, due in 3 days.
- Add new telemetry to detect warmpool image drift that causes attach failures: owner ci-cd-gpu-team, due in 7 days.

Appendix - troubleshooting snippets and notes:

- Rapidly check per-AZ spare capacity:
  infractl capacity list --region eu-west-1 --filter spare=true --format table

- Short-term move traffic to a different region (manual, higher latency) if cross-AZ capacity is exhausted:
  infractl routing failover --service inference-api --to-region us-east-1 --percent 20 --ttl 10m

- Sample log grep for hot-retry loops from the API gateway:
  kubectl -n api logs deploy/api-gateway | grep -E "retry_attempt|429" | tail -n 200

Notes and rationale:

Burst hedging is a trade-off between cost and reliability. We accept small, measured additional cost to protect latency SLOs and customer experience during short-lived spikes (seconds to minutes). The policy emphasizes: automated first, small hedges, short TTL, and cost reconciliation so we maintain predictable economics.
